blocks.title: See and drive the iOS Simulator without leaving the conversation
blocks.description: Build Apple Apps puts a live iOS Simulator in the activity panel. The AI builds, installs and launches your app, then taps through it by accessibility label while you watch or take over on the same device.

showcase.user_prompt: Run the app and check whether the Settings screen looks right in dark mode.
showcase.assistant_reply: Built and installed on iPhone 17 Pro, switched to dark mode and opened Settings. The live screen is in the panel on the right, and you can tap it directly too.

items.title: Live mirroring
items.description: Watch the simulator screen in the activity panel instead of switching to Simulator.app.

items.title: One device, shared
items.description: Tap and swipe in the panel while the AI works on the same simulator.

items.title: Operates by element
items.description: The AI finds controls through the accessibility tree, not by guessing coordinates from screenshots.

items.title: Built-in development guide
items.description: SwiftUI component patterns, Liquid Glass adoption and performance audits load only when a task needs them.

items.title: Build-to-run loop
items.description: Building, installing, launching, deep links and simulated push notifications happen in one flow.

blocks.title: Compared with letting the AI run Xcode on its own

left.title: Command line only
items: Results are guessed from build logs

right.title: With Build Apple Apps
items: You see the screen right after each change
The AI can read the screen, operate it and check its own work
You can take over the same device at any time

items.title: Install Xcode and the simulator runtime
items.description: The plugin runs on macOS only and uses the simulators you already have in Xcode.

items.title: Install baguette
items.description: Screen mirroring and gesture injection come from the open-source baguette tool. The panel shows the Homebrew command and re-checks after you run it.

items.title: Install and enable Build Apple Apps
items.description: Approve the requested permissions. The plugin starts a local simulator service bound to 127.0.0.1 only.

items.title: Open an Xcode or SwiftPM project
items.description: The Simulator tab appears in the activity panel. Ask the AI to build and run your app.

blocks.content: Earlier Vetta versions shipped this as a built-in plugin. From Vetta 0.5.60 it is installed from the marketplace; your panel settings are kept when you install it again.
